answer: Give every task a hidden twist, like a gale bending each reed a different way, so no two instances are alike. A lone solver adapts each time; a farm reusing one mind across many identities produces answers that mirror each other too closely, with the same quirks and slips. Compare submitted work for correlated errors rather than identical text: when a cluster's mistakes line up like ivory keys struck by one hand, discount the whole cluster's rewards. Copying then costs more than it earns, because the farm's efficiency is exactly what exposes it.
